title: Genome-wide identification and characterization of wall-associated kinases, molecular docking and polysaccharide elicitation of monoterpenoid indole alkaloids in micro-propagated Catharanthus roseus.
authors: Ahmed, Jawad; Sajjad, Yasar; Latif, Aasia; Lodhi, Mohammad Saeed; Huzafa, Muhammad; Situ, Chen; Ahmad, Raza; Shah, Muhammad Maroof; Hassan, Amjad
one_liner_zh: 该文对长春花WAK激酶家族进行基因组鉴定，并用分子对接研究其与低聚半乳糖醛酸的结合，虽涉及蛋白-配体对接，但对象为激酶-糖而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅提及ORCA3转录因子表达变化，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Wall-associated kinases (WAKs) are a unique family of proteins that are predominantly localized on the plasma membrane and simultaneously bound to the cell wall. WAKs play a pivotal role in signal transduction to regulate growth, defense, and response to environmental stimuli in plants. These kinases have been identified and characterized in various plant species, however, similar information for Catharanthus roseus is scarce. C. roseus is an evergreen ornamental plant that produces a repertoire of biologically active compounds. The plant is best characterized for the production of antineoplastic monoterpenoid indole alkaloids (MIAs) namely vinblastine and vincristine. Owing to the diverse composition of phytochemicals, C. roseus is known as a "model non-model" plant for secondary metabolite research. Genome analyses showed 37 putative CrWAK genes present in C. roseus, largely localized on the plasma membrane. Phylogenetic analysis revealed six clusters of CrWAKs. Diverse cis-acting elements, including those involved in defense responses, were identified on the promotor regions of CrWAK genes. The highest binding affinity (- 12.6 kcal/mol) was noted for CrWAK-22 against tri-galacturonic acid. Tri-galacturonic acid stimulated 2.5-fold higher production of vinblastine, sixfold upregulation of the expression of ORCA3 transcription factor, and 6.14-fold upregulation of CrWAK-22 expression. Based on these results it was concluded that the expression of CrWAK genes induced by biotic elicitors may have an important role in the production of MIAs. The current findings may serve as a basis for functional characterization and mechanistic explanation of the role of CrWAK genes in the biosynthesis of MIAs upon elicitation.
abstract_zh: 壁相关激酶（WAKs）是一类独特的蛋白质家族，主要定位于质膜上，并同时与细胞壁结合。WAKs在植物中通过信号转导调控生长、防御及对环境刺激的响应中发挥关键作用。这些激酶已在多种植物物种中被鉴定和表征，然而，关于长春花（Catharanthus roseus）的类似信息却较为匮乏。长春花是一种常绿观赏植物，能产生一系列具有生物活性的化合物。该植物以产生抗肿瘤的单萜吲哚生物碱（MIAs），即长春碱和长春新碱而著称。鉴于其植物化学物质组成的多样性，长春花被称为次生代谢物研究中的“模式非模式”植物。基因组分析显示，长春花中存在37个推定的CrWAK基因，主要定位于质膜上。系统发育分析揭示了CrWAKs的六个簇。在CrWAK基因的启动子区域鉴定出多种顺式作用元件，包括参与防御反应的元件。CrWAK-22对三半乳糖醛酸的最高结合亲和力为-12.6 kcal/mol。三半乳糖醛酸刺激长春碱产量提高2.5倍，ORCA3转录因子表达上调6倍，CrWAK-22表达上调6.14倍。基于这些结果，得出结论：由生物诱导子诱导的CrWAK基因表达可能在MIAs的产生中发挥重要作用。当前发现可为CrWAK基因在诱导条件下MIAs生物合成中的功能表征和机制解释提供基础。
